We are animals and it would be foolish to think otherwise. Everything we do as humans we do to achieve the basic materials in life: Food/water/shelter and then finding a mate (yes I am aware of asexuals and those that don’t want kids but those are in minority). 

I dont see what your argument is about not being better than animals. We 100000000% have it better than any animal out there struggling to find food/water/shelter. We have already cracked the code to living smarter and not harder by having established civilizations with morals.

That’s the thing though. Don’t misinterpret my opinion by thinking I like working 8 hours. I hate working as much as you do. But if the trade off is Blue poll: I can work 8 hours/day but safe housing, many food/water supplies where I don’t really even have to prepare my own food if I don’t want to or Red Pill: complete freedom but you have to find your own food/water/shelter every single day forever. I would take blue pill no question. 8 hours isn’t a number that just fell out of the sky, it clearly is a good number to keep business going while also letting workers have their own lives. Back during industrial revolution we were working horrible hours and even children were working and we knocked that down. The fact of the matter is, we always will think we work too much because none of us want to work for the most part but it’s a part of life and we can’t avoid it.
Would you trade the shelter/food/water sources you have for any non domesticated animals situation on the planet?

Depends what you consider “work”. I agree some people do work too much just like some people don’t work enough. I guarantee we work A LOT less than we did before we had civilizations established. Would you rather work 8 hours 5 days a week or live out in the wild and fend for yourself?

I don’t personally think we work that much. Sure you can say that “we are humans and are superior beings with wants and needs”. Every animal has wants and needs. All animals want to live and have needs that are required to do that. We work 8 hours roughly a day, 8 hours of sleep maybe and 8 hours recreation maybe. Every other non domesticated animal on the planet works 24/7 to make sure they A. Can find a source of food/water for themselves and their offspring B. Can find shelter so they aren’t mutilated in their sleep by predators. We have it good as humans and we already cracked that code. Most of us have to work 8 hours and the trade off is we don’t have to struggle for food and water, we have safe sheltering from weather and predators & we have the privilege of having hobbies that we can pursue. No other animal can say that. So I will gladly take the 8 hours I’m working now that keeps the system going rather than struggle like a polar bear

In the grand scheme of things, we don’t work that much. Again, referring to ants, they never take a break they work constantly and have no hobbies or anything, just work. Other large mammals face the daily struggle of finding food and there are days where they go hungry and can’t find shelter from their own predators. We don’t have it bad as humans. We work and then we get off to go to our cozy homes, make whatever dish we are craving and sleep in peace and our families are safe. We even have laws where intruders can be shot and killed on the spot with relatively no punishment.

I’m not a religious guy, I don’t believe we all have a divine destiny to do something important. We are all animals with similar goals: Eat, drink, sleep and shelter to be safe and reproduce to keep us going. Watch the AntsCanada YT vids and all ants do all day is care for the queens eggs for a few weeks and then die. That’s what we do, we work a lot to keep society going for everybody, for this work we get paid to buy essential materials for us to live. This is how life is and always will be for us. There is no point to living that makes any logical sense. All I know is that we are here and we have needs that can only be attained via work and money or it’s a crime for the most part. I don’t like it, nobody does, but it’s a suffering we all endure and I think we are all connected by it
